title: One published contract for jellyscale's own API
description: Serves Goal 3: "Octave's features have the server they need."; "Their app keeps working.". D-110. All of M1 is in it before JS-184 starts, so Octave builds early. D-148: the contract is OpenAPI 3.1.
acceptanceCriteria: One published, versioned contract describes jellyscale's own API. The server serves it to anyone, the repository holds it, and each image carries and serves the contract it was built with.
A client learns the server's identity, version, API version and capabilities, each with its state, without signing in.

Every refusal and failure on jellyscale's own API, including an unknown route, a wrong method, a missing sign-in and a server failure, carries a reason from one closed, versioned list. Each entry gives its meaning in words a viewer understands, naming no mechanism (no token, database or worker), and what the viewer can do: nothing, retry, sign in, choose another, or ask the operator. An entry that informs rather than refuses (such as a conversion that loses audio channels) is marked as a note. Within a version, a transport reason (an unknown route, a wrong method, a missing sign-in, a server failure) and a reason of a stable capability are added and never removed or renamed. A reason used only by preview capabilities may be reworded until its capability becomes stable, and the task that marks it stable locks it. A client generated from the contract is not broken by a reason it does not know. An action a client does not know never breaks it, checked with a client generated from the contract decoding an unknown action.

Each capability is declared, preview or stable (D-134). A declared capability is not served and is refused with its own reason. The server will not start with a route it serves that the contract lacks, with a route it serves marked declared, or with a declared capability it serves. Everything this task serves is preview. playback-info, user-configuration and track-preferences are marked as leaving at the cutover and can never be marked stable.

No capability can be marked stable until a CI check fails on an incompatible change to it (a field, route or reason removed, renamed or narrowed). The task that first marks a capability stable shows that failure.

A conformance check in CI, against a real Postgres, sends each served operation valid and refused requests. It fails on any answer the contract does not allow and on any route the contract does not declare. It is proven on the routes served today plus one declared operation.
Every contract change reaches Octave as a from:jellyscale issue that says what changed and what each platform must do, before the server serves it (D-132). Checked in review.
notes: Cross-project need (D-132): Its M1 part follows Octave's approved M1 designs where Octave has them (ASK-3). A capability no design has yet confirmed ships as preview and becomes stable when Octave confirms it, so the contract never waits on another product. Split by D-20261127-contract-split: M1 content is JS-216.
